Definition: Links an entity/process to an attribute or characteristic it possesses. Qualitative property only.
Example: lake HAS_PROPERTY temperature; plants HAS_PROPERTY medicinal

Definition: Links an entity or property to a process or change it undergoes or carries out.
Example: species richness HAS_PROCESS decrease; plants HAS_PROCESS growth
Comment: Use it to attach a change (increase, decline, shift) to the quantity that changes. Definition drafted by Claude on 2026-11-03 from the annotations; to be reviewed by Mark and Davnah.

Definition: Links an entity to a functional, ecological, or social role it fulfils.
Example: mountain system HAS_ROLE refuge; species HAS_ROLE pollinator

Definition: Links an entity, property or measurement to its explicitly stated numeric value: a count, measure, percentage or range. The number is its own QUANTITATIVE PROPERTY span.
Example: abundance HAS_VALUE 200; species HAS_VALUE 28; elevation HAS_VALUE 2456 m
Comment: Agreed on 2026-11-03: numbers are split from the noun they count and linked with HAS_VALUE, not HAS_PROPERTY.

Definition: Indicates set, taxonomic, population, or categorical inclusion.
Example: Diptera SUBSET_OF insects; endemic species SUBSET_OF regional species
Comment: If we have a species and a group of species, use SUBSET_OF

Definition: Indicates a physical, structural, or compositional part–whole relationship.
Example: leaf PART_OF plant; tributary PART_OF river system
Comment: PART_OF only for a concrete part of the entire object.

Definition:
Indicates the spatial location of an entity within a geographic entity or spatial unit.
Indicates that an organism, population, process, or phenomenon occurs under or within an ecological/environmental context
Example:
Mont Blanc LOCATED_IN European Alps; species LOCATED_IN northern Chile
species LOCATED_IN grassland; plants LOCATED_IN high altitudes
fish LOCATED_IN lake; endemic species LOCATED_IN forest

Definition: Links an event, process, state, or phenomenon to a temporal period.
Example: flowering OCCURS_DURING spring; migration OCCURS_DURING April

Definition: Identifies the geographical or conceptual starting point of a movement, lineage, or process.
Example: migration HAS_ORIGIN Sahel

Definition: Identifies the endpoint or destination of a movement or directed process.
Example: migration HAS_DESTINATION Denmark

Definition: Identifies where an event, process, period or range starts: its start time, start point, or lower bound.
Example: migration HAS_START April; elevational bands HAS_START 250 m
Comment: Replaces STARTS (guide v1). For where a movement comes from, use HAS_ORIGIN. Definition drafted by Claude on 2026-11-03 from the annotations; to be reviewed by Mark and Davnah.

Definition: Identifies where an event, process, period or range ends: its end time, end point, or upper bound.
Example: migration HAS_END May; elevational range HAS_END 5104 m a.s.l.
Comment: Replaces ENDS (guide v1). For where a movement goes, use HAS_DESTINATION. Definition drafted by Claude on 2026-11-03 from the annotations; to be reviewed by Mark and Davnah.

Definition: Indicates that an organism, person, or system uses another entity as a resource, substrate, habitat, food, or for another purpose.
Example: Aymara doctors USES medicinal plants; herbivores USES vegetation

Definition: Indicates that one entity, state, or land-cover type takes the place of another.
Example: grassland REPLACES forest

Definition: Links an observation, finding, pattern, or proposition to a conclusion, implication, or interpretation that it points toward, supports, or provides evidence for.
Example: vegetation belts INDICATES precipitation; species richness pattern INDICATES energy richness hypothesis
Comment: Example added by Claude on 2026-11-03 from the annotations; to be reviewed by Mark and Davnah.

Definition: Indicates a general, non-specific association between entities or phenomena.
Example:
grassland ASSOCIATED_WITH mountain system;
vicariance ASSOCIATED_WITH biogeographic barriers

Definition: Indicates an explicitly stated statistical correlation or correlational relationship.
Example: diversity CORRELATES_WITH elevation

Definition: Indicates that the subject increases as the object increases: a positive directional relation between two quantities, or between a quantity and a gradient.
Example: growth INCREASES_WITH temperature; species richness INCREASES_WITH habitat area
Comment: For a quantity that falls as the other rises, use DECREASES_WITH. Definition drafted by Claude on 2026-11-03 from the annotations; to be reviewed by Mark and Davnah.

Definition: Indicates that the subject decreases as the object increases: a negative directional relation between two quantities, or between a quantity and a gradient.
Example: species richness DECREASES_WITH elevation; body size DECREASES_WITH temperature
Comment: Use instead of INCREASES_WITH with the property Negative_polarity. Definition drafted by Claude on 2026-11-03 from the annotations; to be reviewed by Mark and Davnah.

Definition: Compares two quantities, magnitudes, rates, effects, or other ordered values and asserts that the first is greater.
Example: [Culicidae abundance LOCATED_IN warmer lakes] GREATER_THAN [Culicidae abundance LOCATED_IN cooler lakes]

Definition: Compares two quantities, magnitudes, rates, effects, or other ordered values and asserts that the first is smaller.
Example: [fish abundance LOCATED_IN acidic lakes] LESS_THAN [fish abundance LOCATED_IN neutral lakes]

Definition: Indicates similarity between entities, properties, communities, patterns, or processes.
Example: community SIMILAR_TO community

Definition: Indicates that entities, properties, communities, patterns, or processes are identical
Example: colour SAME_AS colour

Definition: Indicates that two entities, properties, communities, or processes differ.
Example: community DIFFERS_FROM community

Definition: Indicates participation of subject in a process, either actively or passively
Example: common cranes PARTICIPATES_IN migration

Definition: Indicates an interaction between two entities, variables, processes, or drivers.
Example: temperature INTERACTS_WITH predator presence

Definition: Indicates a causal relationship in which the subject produces or brings about the object.
Example: habitat loss CAUSES decline; predation CAUSES mortality

Definition: Indicates that one entity/process influences or has an effect on another without necessarily asserting causality.
Example: temperature AFFECTS abundance; predators AFFECT insect emergence

Definition: Indicates that the subject facilitates or makes the object/process possible.
Example: habitat complexity ENABLES coexistence

Definition: Links an entity to an action or process that acts on it: the entity is what is affected, moved, detected or changed (the object of the verb).
Example: seeds OBJECT_OF carry; crested porcupine OBJECT_OF detected
Comment: The entity that performs the action is linked with PARTICIPATES_IN. Definition drafted by Claude on 2026-11-03 from the annotations; to be reviewed by Mark and Davnah.
